semin-durr:2-2.t:
In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.
His saying: {تَنزِيلٌ}: It may be the khabar (predicate) of «حم» on the view that it is a name of the sūra; or the predicate of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "this is a revelation"; or a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is «كتابٌ فُصِّلَتْ».

semin-durr:3-3.t:
His saying: {كِتَابٌ}: It has preceded that it may be the khabar (predicate) of «تَنْزيل»; it may be a second predicate; it may be a badal (substitute) for «تَنْزيل»; and it may be a fāʿil (agent) of the maṣdar (verbal noun), namely «تنزيلٌ», i.e. "a Book has been sent down" — so said Abū al-Baqāʾ. And «فُصِّلَتْ آياتُه» is a ṣifa (adjective) of «كتاب».
His saying: «قُرْآناً»: There are six aspects in its accusative. First: it is itself a ḥāl (circumstantial), and «عربيَّاً» is its adjective. [Second:] or it is a preparatory ḥāl (ḥāl muwaṭṭiʾa), the ḥāl in reality being «عربيَّاً», and it is a non-transitory ḥāl; the possessor of the ḥāl is either «كتابٌ», because it is described by «فُصِّلَتْ», or «آياته». [Third:] or it is accusative as a maṣdar, i.e. "you recite it as a recitation." [Fourth:] or by way of specification (ikhtiṣāṣ) and praise. [Fifth:] or it is a second object of «فُصِّلَتْ». [Sixth:] or it is accusative by an implied verb, i.e. "We have set it out in detail as a Qurʾān."
His saying: «لقومٍ»: There are three aspects in it. First: it is attached to «فُصِّلَتْ», i.e. it has been set out in detail for these people and made clear to them, because they are the ones who benefit from it, even if it is in itself set out in detail for all people. Second: it is attached to an omitted [word] as an adjective of «قُرآناً», i.e. "being for these people in particular," for what has preceded regarding the meaning. Third: it is attached to «تَنْزِيلٌ»; this is when «من الرحمنِ» is not made an adjective of it, because if you make «من الرحمن» its adjective you will have made a described maṣdar govern; and when «كتابٌ» is neither a predicate of it nor a substitute for it, lest it entail predicating about the mawṣūl (the governing maṣdar, treated like a relative) or substituting for it before its ṣila is complete. Whoever is lenient with the adverbial and its equivalent (the prepositional phrase) pays no attention to any of that. As for when you make «من الرحمن» attached to it and «كتاب» its agent, that does no harm, because it is among its complements and not something extraneous. This passage is among those that display the beauty of the science of iʿrab and train you in many of its chapters.

semin-durr:4-4.t: His saying: {بَشِيراً وَنَذِيراً}: They may be two naʿts (adjectives) of «قُرْآناً», and they may be two ḥāls (circumstantials), either from «كتاب», or from «آياته», or from the pronoun intended in «قُرْآناً». Zayd ibn ʿAlī read both in the nominative, as adjectives of «كتاب», or as the predicate of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "it is a bearer of good tidings and a warner."

semin-durr:5-5.t:
His saying: {في أَكِنَّةٍ}: Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: why was it not said 'on our hearts are coverings,' as it was said 'and in our ears is deafness,' so that the speech would be in one pattern? I say: it is in one pattern, because there is no difference in meaning between your saying 'our hearts are in coverings' and 'on our hearts are coverings'; the proof of this is His saying, Exalted is He: {وَجَعَلْنَا على قُلُوبِهِمْ أَكِنَّةً} [al-Anʿām: 25]; had it been said 'We have put their hearts in coverings,' the meaning would not have differed. And you see that those of them with natural talent do not regard correspondence and attentiveness except in meanings." The Shaykh said: "«في» here is more forceful than «على», because they intended an excess in non-acceptance through their hearts being in coverings that enclose them as a container encloses its contents, so that nothing can reach them, as you say 'the money is in the purse,' unlike your saying 'on the money is a purse,' which does not indicate enclosure and non-access the way a container does. As for «وجعلنا», it is part of Allah the Exalted's reporting, so it does not need exaggeration." The explanation of «الأَكنَّة» and «الوقر» has preceded.
Ṭalḥa read it with kasra on the wāw [«وِقْر»], and the difference between the two has preceded.
His saying: «ممَّا تَدْعُوْنا»: «مِنْ» in «ممَّا» and in «ومِنْ بَيْنِنا» is for the beginning of the extent. So the meaning is that the veil begins from us and begins from you, so the intervening distance between our side and your side is completely filled, with no gap in it. Had «مِنْ» not come, the meaning would be that a veil exists in the middle between the two sides, whereas the intent is exaggeration by excessive separation; for that reason «مِنْ» was brought — so said al-Zamakhsharī. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is construed according to the meaning, because the meaning is: in coverings veiled from hearing what you call us to. It is not permissible for it to be an adjective of «أكنَّة», because the coverings are veils, and veils are not among what they are called to."

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying: {قُلْ}: Ibn Waththāb and al-Aʿmash read «قال», a past verb, as a report about the Messenger. The written form allows both, and the like of this has preceded in al-Anbiyāʾ and at the end of al-Muʾminūn. Al-Aʿmash and al-Nakhaʿī read «يُوْحِي» with kasra on the ḥāʾ, i.e. [the agent being] Allah the Exalted.
His saying: «فاسْتَقِيموا إليه»: It is made transitive with «إلى» because it implies the meaning of "turn yourselves," and the meaning is: direct your uprightness towards Him.

semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying: {غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ}: It has been said: not diminished; they cited for Dhū al-Iṣbaʿ al-ʿAdwānī:
3946 - إني لَعَمْرُكَ ما بابي بذي غَلقٍ ... على الصديقِ ولا خَيْري بمَمْنُوْنِ
(By your life, my door is not locked against a friend, nor is my bounty diminished.)
It has been said: cut off, from «مَنَنْتُ الحَبْلَ», i.e. I cut the rope; they cited:
3947 - فَضْلَ الجوادِ على الخيلِ البِطاءِ فلا ... يُعْطِي بذلك مَمْنُوْناً ولا نَزِقا
(The excellence of the swift steed over slow horses: in that he gives [a run] neither cut short nor rash.)
And it has been said: «غيرُ ممنونٍ» is from al-mann (reproachful reminding of a favour), because Allah the Exalted's giving is not reproached with reminders; only a created being reminds of his favours.

semin-durr:9-9.t: His saying: {وَتَجْعَلُونَ}: It is conjoined to «لَتَكْفُرون», so it falls within the scope of the interrogation.

semin-durr:10-10.t:
His saying: {وَجَعَلَ}: It is resumptive. It is not permissible to conjoin it to the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, because of the separation between them by something extraneous, namely His saying «وتَجْعلون», which is conjoined to «لَتَكْفرون», as has preceded.
His saying: {في أَرْبَعَةِ أَيَّامٍ}: Its implied form is: in the completion of four days, together with the two preceding days.
Al-Zajjāj said: "in the completion of four days," meaning by the completion the two days. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«في أربعة أيام» is a summing-up of the duration of Allah's creating the earth and what is in it, as if He said: all of that in four complete, even days, without increase or decrease." I say: this is like your saying "I built my house in one day and completed it in two days," i.e. including the first. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "i.e. in the completion of four days; were it not for this implied form, the days would be eight: two days in the first, namely His saying {خَلَقَ الأرض فِي يَوْمَيْنِ}, two days in the last, namely His saying {فَقَضَاهُنَّ سَبْعَ سَمَاوَاتٍ فِي يَوْمَيْنِ}, [and four in the middle, namely His saying {في أَرْبَعَةِ أَيَّامٍ}]."
His saying: «سواءً»: The majority read it in the accusative, and there are several aspects in it. First: it is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) by an implied verb, i.e. "they were made even, an evenness" — so said Makkī and Abū al-Baqāʾ. Second: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the «ها» in «أقواتها», or from the «ها» in «فيها» referring to the earth, or from the earth — so said Abū al-Baqāʾ.
This is questionable, because the meaning is only the description of the days as being even, not the description of the earth as such, and the exegesis came on this basis. This is indicated by the reading «سَواءٍ» in the genitive as an adjective of the muḍāf or the muḍāf ilayhi. Al-Suddī and Qatāda said: «سواءً» means: equal for whoever asks about the matter and inquires about the reality of its occurrence and seeks a lesson in it, for he will find it as Allah the Exalted said. However, Ibn Zayd and a group said something close to the meaning Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned, for they said: its meaning is that the matter of these created things and their benefit is even and prepared for those of mankind who need them; so He expressed "those seeking" by "those asking."
Zayd ibn ʿAlī, al-Ḥasan, Ibn Abī Isḥāq, ʿĪsā, Yaʿqūb and ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd read «سَواءٍ» in the genitive, according to what has preceded, and Abū Jaʿfar in the nominative. There are two aspects in it. First: it is the predicate of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "they are even, neither increasing nor decreasing." Makkī said: "It is nominative as a mubtadaʾ," with its predicate being «للسائلين». This is questionable, in that it begins with an indefinite noun without a justifying factor. Then he said: "in the sense of 'even ones,' for whoever asked, saying: in how many [days] was it created? And it has been said: «للسَّائلين» means for all creatures, because they ask for provision and other things from Allah the Exalted."
His saying: «للسَّائلين»: There are three aspects in it. First: it is attached to «سواء», in the sense of "even for those who ask." Second: it is attached to «قَدَّر», i.e. He determined its provisions in it for the sake of those who seek them, who need them and are nourished. Third: it is attached to an omitted [word], as if it were said: this limitation is for the sake of whoever asked: in how many [days] were the earth and what is in it created?

semin-durr:11-11.t:
Al-dukhān (smoke) is what rises from the flame of fire, and it is borrowed for the vapour seen [rising] from the earth in its drought. Its regular plural of paucity is «أَدْخِنة» and of abundance «دِخْنان», as in «غُراب», «أَغْرِبة» and «غِربان»; they deviated in pluralising it as «دواخِن». It has been said: it is the plural of an implied «داخِنة», by way of figurative attribution. Similar to it is «عُثان» and «عَواثِن».
His saying: «وهي دُخانٌ»: of the category of formal simile, because its form is the form of smoke to the eye.
His saying: «أَتَيْنا»: The majority read «ائْتِيا», an imperative from al-ityān (coming), and «قالتا أَتَيْنا» likewise from it. Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn Jubayr and Mujāhid read «آتِيا قالتا آتَيْنا» with madd in both. There are two aspects in it. First: it is from al-muʾātāh, which is concord, i.e. let each of you two accord with the other in what befits it; to this al-Rāzī and al-Zamakhsharī inclined. So the pattern of «آتِيا» is fāʿilā, like «قاتِلا», and the pattern of «آتَيْنا» is fāʿalnā, like «قاتَلْنا». Second: it is from al-īṭāʾ in the sense of giving, so the pattern of «آتِيا» is afʿilā, like «أَكْرِما», and the pattern of «آتَيْنا» is afʿalnā, like «أَكْرَمْنا». On the first, an object has been omitted; on the second, two objects have been omitted, since the implied form is: "give obedience from yourselves to the One who commanded you." They said: "we have given Him obedience."
Abū al-Faḍl al-Rāzī rejected the second aspect, saying: "«آتَيْنا» with madd is on the pattern fāʿalnā from al-muʾātāh, in the sense of 'we hastened,' with the direct object omitted; it is not from al-īṭāʾ, which is giving, because of the far-fetchedness of omitting both its objects." I say: this is what prevented al-Zamakhsharī from making it from al-īṭāʾ.
His saying: «طَوْعاً أو كَرْهاً»: two maṣdars (verbal nouns) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "obedient or compelled." Al-Aʿmash read «كُرْهاً» with ḍamma. The discussion of that has preceded in al-Nisāʾ.
His saying: «قالتا»: i.e. the heaven and the earth said. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "He meant the two mentioned groups; He made the heavens one heaven and the earths one earth, and it is like the poet's saying:
3948 - ألم يُحْزِنْكَ أنَّ حبالَ قومي ... وقومِك قد تبايَنَتا انْقِطاعا
(Does it not grieve you that the ropes of my people and of your people have parted, severed?)
He expressed them with «تَباينتا» (dual)." The Shaykh said: "It is not as he mentioned, because only the earth in the singular and the heaven in the singular had been mentioned before, so the dual expression was good. As for the verse, it is as if he said 'the two ropes of my people and your people,' and he made «تبايَنَتا» feminine according to the meaning, because by the ropes he meant affection."
His saying: «طائِعِين»: Regarding its coming in the form of the plural of rational masculines there are two aspects. First: what is meant is "the two came with the rational beings and others in them," so He gave precedence to the rational over others; this is the view of al-Kisāʾī. Second: since He treated them as rational beings in reporting about them and commanding them, they were pluralised as such beings are, as in His saying {رَأَيْتُهُمْ لِي سَاجِدِينَ} [Yūsuf: 4]. Is this dialogue literal or figurative? And if figurative, is it a representation (tamthīl) or an imaginative figure (takhyīl)? There is disagreement.

semin-durr:12-12.t:
His saying: {سَبْعَ}: There are four aspects in its accusative. First: it is a second object of «قَضاهُنَّ», because it is made to imply the meaning of "He made them, by His decree, seven heavens."
Second: it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object of «قَضاهُنَّ», i.e. "He fashioned them numbered," with «قضى» in the sense of "made," as in the saying of Abū Dhuʾayb:
3949 - وعليهما مَسْرُوْدتان قَضاهما ... داوُدُ أو صَنَعُ السَّوابغِ تُبَّعُ
(Upon the two of them were two coats of riveted mail that David fashioned, or Tubbaʿ, skilled maker of ample mail.)
i.e. made them. Third: it is a tamyīz (specification). Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It may be that [the pronoun] is a vague pronoun explained by «سبع سماوات» [as a specification]"; by "vague" he means that it does not refer back to «السماء» either in wording or in meaning, unlike its being a ḥāl or a second object. Fourth: it is a badal (substitute) for «هُنَّ» in «فقَضاهُنَّ» — so said Makkī. He also said: "«السَّماء» is masculine and feminine; the Qurʾān came with the feminine, and had it come with the masculine it would have been said «سبعة سماوات»." The verification of its masculine and feminine has preceded at the beginning of al-Baqara.
His saying: «وحِفْظاً»: There are two aspects in its accusative. First: it is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) by an implied verb, i.e. "and We guarded it with the piercing stars, a guarding." Second: it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) according to the meaning, for the implied form is: "We created the stars as adornment and as protection." The Shaykh said: "This is strained and a departure from what is easy and clear."

semin-durr:13-13.t: His saying: {فَإِنْ أَعْرَضُواْ}: an iltifāt (shift of person) from addressing them in His saying «قل أئِنَّكم» to the third person: because they committed turning away, He turned away from addressing them; and this is a fine congruence. The majority read «صاعقَةً مثلَ صاعقةِ» with the alif in both, and Ibn al-Zubayr, al-Nakhaʿī, al-Sulamī and Ibn Muḥayṣin «صَعْقَةً مثلَ صَعْقة» omitting it with sukūn on the ʿayn. The discussion of that has preceded at the beginning of al-Baqara. One says «صَعَقَتْه الصاعقةُ فصَعِقَ» (the thunderbolt struck him and he was struck senseless); this is among what comes with faʿaltuhu — with fatḥa — followed by faʿila with kasra; similar to it is «جَدَعْتُه فَجَدِعَ». «الصَّعْقَة» is the single instance.

semin-durr:14-14.t:
His saying: {إِذْ جَآءَتْهُمُ}: There are several aspects in it. First: it is an adverb of «أَنْذَرْتُكم», as in "I met you when such-and-such was." Second: it is accusative by «صاعقة», because it is in the sense of punishment, i.e. "I have warned you of the punishment that befell at the time their messengers came." Third: it is an adjective of the first «صاعِقَة». Fourth: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the second «صاعقة». Abū al-Baqāʾ stated these two, and both are questionable, since the apparent sense is that the thunderbolt is a body, namely a piece of fire that descends from the sky and burns, as preceded in its explanation at the beginning of this work; so time does not occur as an adjective of it nor as a ḥāl from it, and interpreting it in the sense of punishment takes it out of its denotation without necessity. He made it a description of the first only because it is indefinite, and a ḥāl from the second because it is definite by its annexation to a proper name; had he made it a ḥāl from the first because it is particularised by annexation, it would have been permissible, and so the aspects would become five.
His saying: {مِن بَيْنِ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ}: The apparent sense is that both pronouns refer to ʿĀd and Thamūd. It has been said: the pronoun in «خَلْفِهم» refers to the messengers. This was considered far-fetched in meaning, since the implied form would become: "the messengers came to them from behind the messengers," i.e. from behind themselves. It may be answered that it is of the category of «دِرْهمٌ ونصفُه» ("a dirham and half of it" [meaning half of another]), i.e. and from behind other messengers.
His saying: {أَلاَّ تعبدوا}: Three aspects are possible for «أَنْ». First: it is the lightened form of the heavy [«أنَّ»], its noun being the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and the prohibitive clause after it is the predicate; so the Shaykh parsed it. This is questionable in two respects. First: the lightened form does not occur after a verb except one of the verbs of certainty. Second: the predicate in the chapter of inna and its sisters is not a request; if anything of that sort occurs it is interpreted, and for that reason they interpreted [the poet's saying]:
3950 - إنَّ الذينَ قَتَلْتُمْ أمسِ سَيِّدَهُمْ ... لا تَحْسَبُوا ليلَهم عن ليلِكم ناما
(Those whose chief you killed yesterday — do not think their night has slept away from your night.)
and the other's saying:
3951 - ولو أصابَتْ لقالَتْ وَهْيَ صادِقةٌ ... إنَّ الرِّياضَةَ لا تُنْصِبْكَ للشِّيْبِ
(Had she been right, she would have said, and truthfully: "Exercise — let it not wear you out for grey hair.")
by implying [a verb of] saying. Second: it is the particle that puts the imperfect in the accusative, and the prohibitive clause after it is its ṣila, connected with the prohibition as it is connected with the imperative in «كَتبتُ إليه بأنْ قُمْ» ("I wrote to him to stand"); a difficulty has passed regarding connecting it with the imperative, and the like of it arises with the prohibition. Third: it is explicative (mufassira) of their coming, because it implies [a verb of] saying. «لا» in all these aspects is prohibitive; and it may be negating on the second aspect, with the verb accusative by «أنْ» after the negating «لا», for the negating «لا» does not prevent a governing word from governing what follows it, as in «جئتُ بلا زيدٍ» ("I came without Zayd"). Al-Ḥawfī mentioned nothing else.
His saying: «لو شاءَ»: Al-Zamakhsharī implied the object of «شاء» as: "had He willed the sending of messengers, He would have sent down angels." The Shaykh said: "I examined the Qurʾān and the speech of the Arabs, and I did not find the omission of the object of «شاء» occurring after «لو» except when it is of the same kind as its apodosis, as in:
{وَلَوْ شَآءَ الله لَجَمَعَهُمْ عَلَى الهدى} [al-Anʿām: 35], i.e. had He willed to gather them upon guidance, He would have gathered them upon it; {لَوْ نَشَآءُ لَجَعَلْنَاهُ حُطَاماً} [al-Wāqiʿa: 65]; {لَوْ نَشَآءُ جَعَلْنَاهُ أُجَاجاً} [al-Wāqiʿa: 70]; {وَلَوْ شَآءَ رَبُّكَ لآمَنَ} [Yūnus: 99]; {وَلَوْ شَآءَ رَبُّكَ مَا فَعَلُوهُ} [al-Anʿām: 112]; {لَوْ شَآءَ الله مَا عَبَدْنَا مِن دُونِهِ} [al-Naḥl: 35]. The poet said:
3952 - فلو شاءَ ربِّي كنتُ قيسَ بنَ خالدٍ ... ولو شاءَ ربي كنتُ قيسَ بنَ مَرْثدِ
(Had my Lord willed, I would have been Qays ibn Khālid; had my Lord willed, I would have been Qays ibn Marthad.)
And the rajaz poet said:
3953 - واللذِ لو شاءَ لكنْتُ صَخْراً ... أو جَبَلاً أشمَّ مُشْمَخِرَّا
(By the One who, had He willed, I would have been a rock, or a lofty, towering mountain.)"
He said: "So according to what has been established, the omitted item is not what al-Zamakhsharī implied; the implied form is only: 'had our Lord willed to send down angels with the message from Him to humans, He would have sent them down with it to them.' This is more forceful in refusing the sending of humans, since they made that conditional on the sending down of angels, and He did not will that, so how would He will it in the case of humans?" I say: Abū al-Qāsim's (al-Zamakhsharī's) implied form is more apt in meaning and freer from putting the overt noun in the place of the pronoun, since the implied form [of the Shaykh] becomes: "had He willed to send down angels, He would have sent down angels."
His saying: {بِمَآ أُرْسِلْتُمْ بِهِ}: This is an address to Hūd, Ṣāliḥ and other prophets, peace be upon them, giving precedence to the one addressed over the absent, as in «أنت وزيدٌ تقومان» ("you and Zayd stand"). «ما» may be a relative in the sense of «الذي», its returning pronoun being «به»; or it may be maṣdariyya, i.e. "in your being sent." On this, «به» [refers] to that interpreted maṣdar, and it is of the category of emphasis, as if it were said: "disbelievers in your being sent with it."

semin-durr:16-16.t:
His saying: {صَرْصَراً}: Al-ṣarṣar is the violent wind. It has been said: it is the cold one, from al-ṣirr, which is cold. It has been said: it is the one of intense scorching heat. And it has been said: it is the sounding one, from «صَرَّ البابُ», i.e. the door's creaking was heard. «الصَّرَّة» is the cry, and from it: {فَأَقْبَلَتِ امرأته فِي صَرَّةٍ} [al-Dhāriyāt: 29]. Ibn Qutayba said: "«صَرْصَر» may be from al-ṣirr, which is cold; or from «صَرَّ البابُ»; or from al-ṣarra, which is the cry, and from it: {فَأَقْبَلَتِ امرأته فِي صَرَّةٍ} [al-Dhāriyāt: 29]." Al-Rāghib said: "«صَرْصَر» is a word from al-ṣirr, and that goes back to tightness, because of the knotting [contraction] in coldness."
His saying: «نَحِساتٍ»: The Kufans and Ibn ʿĀmir read it with kasra on the ḥāʾ, and the rest with sukūn. As for the kasra, it is an adjective on the pattern faʿil, and its verb is faʿila, also with kasra on the ʿayn; one says «نَحِس فهو نَحِسٌ», like «فَرِح فهو فَرِحٌ» and «أَشِرَ فهو أَشِرٌ». Al-Layth transmitted from al-Kisāʾī the imāla of its alif because of the kasra, but that is not well known from him, so that al-Dānī attributed it to error.
As for the reading with sukūn, it allows three aspects. First: it is lightened from faʿil in the preceding reading, and in this there is agreement between the two readings. Second: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) used as an adjective, like «رجلٍ عَدْلٍ» ("a just man"); but the plural weakens this, for the eloquent usage with a maṣdar used as an adjective is to keep it singular; it seems what permitted the plural is the difference of its kinds originally. Third: it is an independent adjective on the pattern faʿl with sukūn on the ʿayn. But the morphologists did not mention, among adjectives coming from faʿila with kasra on the ʿayn, other than limited patterns, among which there is no faʿl with sukūn; they mentioned: «فَرِحَ فهو فَرِحٌ», «حَوِرَ فهو أحورُ», «شَبعَ فهو شبعانُ», «سَلِمَ فهو سالمٌ» and «بَلي فهو بالٍ».
On the meaning of «نَحِسات» there are two views. First: they are [days] of ill omen. Al-Suddī said: i.e. ill-omened, from the well-known naḥs. Second: they are intensely cold. For the first meaning they cited the poet's saying:
3954 - يَوْمَيْنِ غَيْمَيْنِ ويوماً شَمْسا ... نَجْمَيْنِ سَعْدَيْنِ ونجماً نَحْسا
(Two cloudy days and a sunny day; two auspicious stars and an ill-omened star.)
And for the second meaning the other's saying:
3955 - كأنَّ سُلافَةً عُرِضَتْ لنَحْسٍ ... يُحِيْلُ شَفيفُها الماءَ الزُّلالا
(As if choice wine were exposed to a cold wind whose biting chill turns clear water [to ice].)
And from it:
3956 - قد أَغْتدي قبلَ طُلوعِ الشمسِ ... للصيدِ في يومٍ قليلِ النَّحْسِ
(I set out early before sunrise to hunt, on a day of little naḥs.)
It has been said that in this verse he means dust by it, i.e. of little dust; and it has been said likewise in the verse [of the Qurʾān] that they were days of dust. «نَحِسات» is a naʿt (adjective) of «أيَّام», and the plural with alif and tāʾ is regular in the adjective of what is not rational, as in «أيامٍ معدوداتٍ». Its verification has preceded in al-Baqara.
«لِنُذِيْقَهُمْ» is attached to «أَرْسَلْنا». It has been read «لِتُذِيقَهم» with the upper-dotted tāʾ.
On the pronoun [in this reading] there are two views; the first: it is the wind, i.e. "so that the wind, or the days, might make them taste," figuratively. [Translator's note: the source mentions only the first of the two views.] «عذاب الخِزْيِ» is an annexation of the qualified noun to its quality; for that reason He said {وَلَعَذَابُ الآخرة أخزى}, since it entails sharing [in the quality] plus excess. Attributing disgrace to the punishment is figurative, because it is its cause.

semin-durr:17-17.t: His saying: {وَأَمَّا ثَمُودُ}: The majority read it in the nominative as a diptote. Al-Aʿmash and Ibn Waththāb [read it] fully declined, and likewise everything in the Qurʾān except His saying {وَآتَيْنَا ثَمُودَ الناقة} [al-Isrāʾ: 59]; they said: because the written form there is «ثمود» without alif. Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn Abī Isḥāq, al-Aʿmash in one transmission and ʿĀṣim in one transmission read «ثمود» in the accusative, fully declined; and al-Ḥasan, Ibn Hurmuz and ʿĀṣim also in the accusative as a diptote. As for full declension and its absence, their justification has preceded in Hūd. As for the nominative, it is as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with the clause after it as the khabar (predicate), and that is necessary according to the majority, because «أمَّا» is followed only by a mubtadaʾ, so preoccupation (ishtighāl) is not permissible in what follows it except rarely, as in this reading. If you imply the verb that puts it in the accusative, imply it after the accusative noun, i.e. "as for Thamūd, We guided them — We guided them"; they said: because verbs do not follow it.

semin-durr:19-19.t: His saying: {وَيَوْمَ يُحْشَرُ}: There are two aspects regarding what governs this adverb. First: an omitted [verb] indicated by what follows, namely His saying «فهم يُوْزَعُون», its implied form being "people are driven on the day ... are gathered"; Abū al-Baqāʾ implied it as "they are held back on the day of the gathering." Second: it is accusative by «اذْكُرْ», i.e. "remember the day." Nāfiʿ read «نَحْشُرُ» with the nūn of majesty and ḍamma on the shīn, with «أعداءَ» in the accusative, i.e. "We gather." The rest [read] with the yāʾ of absence with ḍamma and fatḥa on the shīn, as a verb whose agent is not named, with «أعداءُ» nominative as standing in place of the agent. Al-Aʿraj read the shīn of «نَحْشِر» with kasra. «حتى» is the limit of «يُحْشَر».

semin-durr:22-22.t: His saying: {أَن يَشْهَدَ}: Several aspects are possible in it. First: "from [the fact] that [they] bear witness." Second: "for fear that [they] bear witness." Third: "for the sake of [their] bearing witness"; both [the second and third] are in the sense of the mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose). Fourth: "from [their] bearing witness," i.e. you could not hold back, and it was not possible for you to hide from your limbs and conceal yourselves from them. Fifth: it is made to imply the meaning of supposing, and that is far-fetched.

semin-durr:23-23.t: His saying: {وَذَلِكُمْ ظَنُّكُمُ}: There are several aspects in it. First: «ظنُّكم» is its khabar (predicate), «الذي ظَنَنْتُمْ» is its naʿt (adjective), and «أَرْدَاكم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial), with «قد» implied with it on the view of the majority, contrary to al-Akhfash. Makkī's rejection of the ḥāl reading because of the absence of «قد» is not granted, for the reason I mentioned. Second: «ظنُّكم» is a badal (substitute) and the relative is its predicate, with «أَرْدَاكم» also a ḥāl. Third: the relative is a second predicate. Fourth: «ظَنُّكم» is a substitute or an explicative apposition (bayān), the relative is the predicate, and «أَرْداكم» is a second predicate. Fifth: «ظَنُّكم», the relative and the clause «أَرْداكم» are [all] predicates. However, the Shaykh rejected al-Zamakhsharī's statement "«ظنُّكم» and «أَرْدَاكم» are two predicates." He said: "Because His saying «وذلكم» points to their earlier supposition, so the implied form becomes: 'your supposition about your Lord that He does not know is your supposition about your Lord'; so from the predicate is gained what is gained from the subject, and that is not permissible. This is parallel to what the grammarians forbade in your saying 'the master of the slave-girl is her owner.'" Ibn ʿAṭiyya forbade «أَرْداكم» being a ḥāl because «قد» is absent, and the disagreement about that has preceded.

semin-durr:24-24.t:
His saying: {يَسْتَعْتِبُواْ}: The majority read it with fatḥa on the yāʾ and kasra on the second tāʾ, active; and {فَمَا هُم مِّنَ المعتبين} with fatḥa on the tāʾ as a passive participle. Its meaning is: if they seek al-ʿutbā, which is being pleased with [i.e. reconciliation], they are not among those to whom it is granted. It has been said: the meaning is: if they seek the removal of what they are reproached for, they are not among those whose request to remove the reproach is answered.
The origin of al-ʿatab is a place remote [and hard] for one who alights there; from it the threshold of a door and the step are called «عَتَبة». Al-ʿatab is used to express the harshness a person finds in his breast against his companion. «عَتَبْتُ فلاناً» means I showed him harshness, and «أَعْتَبْتُه» means I removed his grievance, like «أَشْكَيْتُه»; and it has been said: I provoked him to reproach.
Al-Ḥasan and ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd read «وإن يُسْتَعْتَبوا», passive, and {فَمَا هُم مِّنَ المعتبين} as an active participle, meaning: if they are asked to give satisfaction, they will not do that, because they have left the abode of moral obligation. It has been said its meaning is: if what they are not reproached for is sought, they are not among those who remove the grievance. Abū Dhuʾayb said:
3957 - أَمِنَ المَنُونِ ورَيْبِه تَتَوَجَّعُ ... والدهرُ ليسَ بمُعْتِبٍ مَنْ يَجْزَعُ
(Do you grieve at death and its vicissitudes? Time does not appease one who frets.)

semin-durr:25-25.t:
His saying: {وَقَيَّضْنَا}: The origin of al-taqyīḍ is facilitating and preparing. «قَيَّضْتُه له لكذا» means I prepared him and facilitated him. «هذان ثوبان قَيْضان» means each of the two garments is equivalent to the other in price. Al-muqāyaḍa is exchange (barter). His saying {نُقَيِّضْ لَهُ شَيْطَاناً} [al-Zukhruf: 36] means: We make it easy for him to take hold of him as the shell (al-qayḍ) takes hold of the egg. Al-qayḍ originally is the outer shell of the egg.
His saying: «في أُمَمٍ»: in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «عليهم», the meaning being: "being among the totality of nations." This is like the saying:
3958 - إنْ تَكُ عَنْ أَحْسَنِ الصَّنيعةِ مَأْ ... فُوْكاً ففي آخَرين قد أَفِكُوا
(If you have been turned away from the finest deed, then [you are] among others who were turned away.)
i.e. among a group of other people. It has been said: «في» is in the sense of "with."

semin-durr:26-26.t: His saying: {والغوا}: The majority read it with fatḥa on the ghayn. It allows two aspects. First: it is from «لَغِي» with kasra, «يَلْغَى». In this there are two meanings: one, from «لَغِيَ» when one speaks idle talk (al-laghw), which is that in which there is no benefit; the other, from «لَغِي بكذا», i.e. he threw it, so «في» would be in the sense of the bāʾ, i.e. "throw it and cast it aside." The second of the two original aspects: it is from «لَغا» with fatḥa, «يَلْغَى» also with fatḥa, as al-Akhfash related; its regular form would have been ḍamma, like «غزا يَغْزو», but it was given fatḥa because of the guttural letter. Qatāda, Abū Ḥaywa, Abū al-Sammāl, al-Zaʿfarānī, Ibn Abī Isḥāq and ʿĪsā read it with ḍamma on the ghayn, from «لَغا» with fatḥa, «يَلْغُو», like «دَعا يَدْعُو». In the ḥadīth: «فقد لَغَوْتَ» ("then you have spoken idly"), and this accords with the reading of other than the majority.

semin-durr:28-28.t:
His saying: {ذَلِكَ}: There are two aspects in it. First: it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «جزاءُ» is its khabar (predicate). Second: it is the predicate of an omitted subject, i.e. "the matter is that," and {جَزَآءُ أَعْدَآءِ الله النار} is an independent clause explaining the clause before it.
His saying: «النارُ»: There are three aspects in it. First: it is a badal (substitute) for «جزاء»; this is questionable, since the substitute takes the place of what it substitutes for, so the implied form would become "that is the Fire." Second: it is the predicate of an implied subject. Third: it is a mubtadaʾ, and {لَهُمْ فِيهَا دَارُ الخُلْدِ} is the khabar. «دارُ» may be nominative as a fāʿil (agent) or as a mubtadaʾ.
His saying {فِيهَا دَارُ الخُلْدِ} requires that «دارُ الخلد» be other than the Fire, yet the matter is not so; rather the Fire is itself the abode of eternity. This was answered by saying that a thing may be made a container of itself with respect to what relates to it, by way of exaggeration, as if that related thing became a place of settlement for it; and this is more forceful than attributing the related thing to it by way of predication. Like it is the saying:
3959 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... وفي اللَّهِ إنْ لم يُنْصِفُوا حَكَمٌ عَدْلُ
(… and in Allah, if they do not deal fairly, is a just judge.)
and His saying, Exalted is He: {لَّقَدْ كَانَ لَكُمْ فِي رَسُولِ الله أُسْوَةٌ حَسَنَةٌ} [al-Aḥzāb: 21], while the Messenger, peace be upon him, is himself the example. So they answered. This is questionable, since the apparent sense — and it is a sound, transmitted meaning — is that within the Fire there is an abode called the abode of eternity, with the Fire surrounding it.
His saying: «جَزاءً»: There are three aspects in its accusative. First: it is accusative by an implied verb, being an emphasising maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "they are recompensed with a recompense." Second: it is accusative by the maṣdar before it, namely {جَزَآءُ أَعْدَآءِ الله}, a maṣdar being put in the accusative by its like, as in His saying: {فَإِنَّ جَهَنَّمَ جَزَآؤُكُمْ جَزَاءً} [al-Isrāʾ: 63]. Third: it is accusative as a maṣdar standing in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial). «بما» is attached to the second «جَزاء» if it is not emphasising, and to the first if it is. «بآياتِنا» is attached to «يَجْحَدون».

semin-durr:29-29.t: The disagreement over «أَرِنا» and over the nūn of «اللذَيْنِ» has preceded. Al-Khalīl said: "If you say «أَرِني ثوبَك» with kasra, its meaning is 'let me see it'; and with sukūn, 'give it to me.'" Al-Zamakhsharī said: "i.e. for what they used to talk idly," so He mentioned denial (al-juḥūd) because it is the cause of the idle talk — end of quote. He means it is of the category of putting the cause in place of the effect, and that is an acceptable figure of speech.

semin-durr:30-30.t:
His saying: {ثُمَّ استقاموا}: «ثم» is for the distance of rank in excellence.
His saying: {أَلاَّ تَخَافُواْ}: «أَنْ» may be the lightened [form of «أنَّ»], or the explicative, or the one that puts [the verb] in the accusative. «لا» is prohibitive on the first two aspects and negating on the third. The difficulty in that has preceded. The implied form is «بأنْ لا تَخافوا», i.e. with the absence of fear. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The implied form is «بأَنْ لا تَخافوا», or 'saying: «أن لا تخافوا»'; on the first it is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. they descended with their saying 'do not fear'; on the second the ḥāl is omitted." I say: he means that the implied bāʾ is circumstantial, so the ḥāl is not omitted, while on the second the ḥāl is the implied [verb of] saying. There is laxity in this; otherwise the ḥāl is omitted in both places, and just as the thing said stands in the place of the ḥāl, so the prepositional phrase stands in its place.
ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] read «لا تَخافوا» dropping «أنْ», which is by implying [a verb of] saying, i.e. "saying: do not fear."

semin-durr:32-32.t:
His saying: {نُزُلاً}: There are several aspects in it. First: it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the relative noun or from its returning pronoun. What is meant by al-nuzul is the provision prepared for the one who alights [the guest], as if it were said: "and for you in it is what you request, being prepared." Second: it is a ḥāl from the agent of «تَدَّعُوْن», or from the pronoun in «لكم», on the basis that «نُزُلاً» is the plural of «نازِل», like «صابِر» and «صُبُر», «شارِف» and «شُرُف». Third: it is an emphasising maṣdar (verbal noun). This is questionable, because the maṣdar of «نَزَل» is «النزول», not «النُّزُل». It has been said: it is the maṣdar of «أَنْزَل».
His saying: «مِنْ غَفَورٍ»: It may be attached to an omitted [word] as an adjective of «نُزُلاً»; it may be attached to «تَدَّعون», i.e. "you seek it from the One who is Forgiving, Merciful"; and it may be attached to the [notion of] settledness to which the prepositional phrase in «لكم» is attached, i.e. "it is settled for you from the Forgiving, Merciful." Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "So it would be a ḥāl from «ما»." I say: this inference of his is not clear; rather it is attached to the settledness as an adjunct (faḍla) like other adjuncts, and it is not a ḥāl from «ما».

semin-durr:33-33.t: His saying: {وَقَالَ إِنَّنِي}: The majority read «إنني» with two nūns, and Ibn Abī ʿAbla and Ibn Nūḥ with one nūn.

semin-durr:34-34.t:
His saying: {وَلاَ السيئة}: There are two aspects regarding this «لا». First: it is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis, as in His saying {وَلاَ الظل وَلاَ الحرور} [Fāṭir: 21] and His saying {وَلاَ المسياء} [Ghāfir: 58], because «استوى» is not satisfied with one [item]. Second: it is foundational, not emphatic, since what is meant by «الحسنة» and «السيئة» is the genus, i.e. good deeds are not equal among themselves, for they vary, nor are evil deeds equal either, for one may be greater than another; this is taken from the words of al-Zamakhsharī. The Shaykh said: "If you take «الحسنة» and «السيئة» as a genus, its redundancy would not be like its redundancy in the preceding aspect." I say: so he made it redundant in the second meaning as well, and that is questionable for what has preceded.
His saying: «كأنَّه وليٌّ»: There are two aspects regarding this simile clause. First: it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), the relative noun being a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «إذا» of surprise its khabar (predicate); what governs this adverb, namely the [notion of] settledness, is what governs this ḥāl, and the point of benefit in this speech is the ḥāl. The implied form is: "then, there present, is the enemy, resembling the affectionate close friend." Second: the relative noun is also a mubtadaʾ, the clause after it is its khabar, and «إذا» is governed by the meaning of the simile, an adverb being allowed to precede its abstract governor. This is if it is said that it is an adverb; if it is said that it is a particle, there is no governor.

semin-durr:35-35.t: His saying: {وَمَا يُلَقَّاهَا}: The majority read «يُلَقَّاها», from al-talqiya (being granted). Ibn Kathīr in one transmission and Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif [read] «يُلاقاها», from al-mulāqāh (meeting). The pronoun refers to the trait, or the word, or Paradise, or the testimony of divine oneness.

semin-durr:37-37.t: His saying: {خَلَقَهُنَّ}: There are three aspects regarding this pronoun. First: it refers to the four conjoined items. As for the pronoun coming like the pronoun of feminines — as al-Zamakhsharī said — it is because the plural of what is non-rational takes the rule of the feminine singular or of feminines, as in «الأقلامُ بَرَيْتُها وبَرَيْتُهنَّ» ("the pens, I sharpened them [fem. sg. / fem. pl.]"). The Shaykh disputed this with him, in that he did not distinguish between the plural of paucity and the plural of abundance in that respect, because the most eloquent usage with the plural of paucity is to treat it as feminines, and with the plural of abundance to treat it as a feminine singular; so the most eloquent is to say «الأجذاعُ كَسَرْتُهُنَّ» and «الجذوعُ كَسَرْتُها». What preceded in this verse is not a plural of paucity — I mean in a single word — but He mentioned four conjoined items, so they were given the status of a plural expressed by a single word. I say: al-Zamakhsharī is not in the position of explaining the eloquent and the more eloquent, but rather how the pronoun came as a pronoun of feminines after three masculine things and one feminine thing had preceded, the rule being to give precedence to the masculine over the feminine. [Second:] or, since He said «ومِنْ آياته», they were in the sense of "the signs," so it was said «خلقهنَّ»; al-Zamakhsharī also mentioned this, that it refers to the word «الآيات». Third: it refers to the sun and the moon, because two is a plural, and the plural is feminine, and because of their saying «شموس وأقمار» (suns and moons).

semin-durr:41-41.t:
His saying: {إِنَّ الذين كَفَرُواْ}: There are six aspects regarding its khabar (predicate). First: it is mentioned, namely His saying «أولئك ينادَوْن». Bilāl ibn Abī Burda was asked about that in his recounted story, and he said: "I find no way through it." Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ said to him: "It is close to you: «أولئك ينادَوْن»." This was considered far-fetched from two respects. First: the many intervening separations. Second: the prior mention of one to whom the pointing in «أولئك» can soundly refer, namely His saying {والذين لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ}, and the demonstrative refers to the nearest thing mentioned.
Second: it is omitted because the meaning is understood, and it was implied as "will be punished," or "will be destroyed," or "are obstinate." Al-Kisāʾī said: "What preceded in the speech before «إنَّ» fills its place, namely His saying {أَفَمَن يلقى فِي النار}." I say: he means in indicating it, the implied form being "will abide forever in the Fire." ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar asked ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd about that, and he said: "Its meaning in exegesis is: those who disbelieved in the Reminder when it came to them disbelieved in it." So he implied the predicate from the same kind as the ṣila (relative clause). This is questionable, in that the predicate and what it is predicated of become one in meaning without added benefit, as in «سيدُ الجاريةِ مالكُها» ("the master of the slave-girl is her owner").
Third: the second «الذين» is a badal (substitute) for the first «إنَّ الذين», and what is predicated of the substitute is predicated of what it substitutes for, so it follows that the predicate is {لاَ يَخْفَوْنَ عَلَيْنَآ}. This is extracted from the words of al-Zamakhsharī. [Translator's note: the second «الذين» meant here is that of {إِنَّ الذين يُلْحِدُونَ فِي آيَاتِنَا} in the preceding verse.]
Fourth: the predicate is His saying {لاَّ يَأْتِيهِ الباطل}, the returning pronoun being omitted, its implied form being "falsehood does not come to it from them," as in «السَّمْنُ مَنَوان بدرهم» ("ghee: two manas for a dirham"), i.e. two manas of it. Or «أل» is a substitute for the pronoun on the view of the Kufans, its implied form being: "those who disbelieved in the Reminder — their falsehood does not come to it."
Fifth: the predicate is His saying {مَّا يُقَالُ لَكَ}, the returning pronoun also being omitted, its implied form being: "those who disbelieved in the Reminder — nothing is said to you concerning them except what was said to the messengers before you." The Shaykh adopted these two aspects.
Sixth: some of the Kufans held that it is His saying {وَإِنَّهُ لَكِتَابٌ عَزِيزٌ}, and this is not intelligible.
The clause «وإنَّه لكتابٌ» is circumstantial, and {لاَّ يَأْتِيهِ الباطل} is an adjective of «كتاب». «تنزيلٌ» is the predicate of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), or an adjective of «كتابٌ», on the basis that «لا يأتيه» is parenthetical, or [that it is] an adjective as preceded, on the view of whoever allows a non-explicit adjective to precede an explicit one; its verification has preceded in al-Māʾida. «مِنْ حكيمٍ» is an adjective of «تَنْزيلٌ» or attached to it. «الباطلُ» is an active participle; and it has been said: a maṣdar (verbal noun), like «العافية» and «العاقبة».

semin-durr:43-43.t: His saying: {إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَذُو مَغْفِرَةٍ}: It has been said: it explains what was said, as if it were said: "it was said to the messengers: indeed your Lord is the Possessor of ..." And it has been said: it is resumptive.

semin-durr:44-44.t:
His saying: {ءَاعْجَمِيٌّ}: The two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] and Abū Bakr read it with full pronunciation of the hamza, and Hishām dropping the first. The rest [read] with easing of the second, between-between (bayna bayna). As for the madd, its rule is known from His saying «أأنذَرْتَهم» at the beginning of this work. Whoever reads it as a question says: its meaning is "a non-Arabic Book and an Arab Messenger?" It has been said: "and an Arab [people] to whom it is sent?" And it has been said: its meaning is "is part of it non-Arabic and part of it Arabic?" Whoever does not keep the interrogative hamza may have omitted it in wording while intending it in meaning, and in that there is agreement of the two readings; but that is not permissible according to the majority unless there is «أم» in the speech, as in:
3960 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... بسَبْعٍ رَمَيْنَ الجَمْرَ أم بثمان
(… did they throw the pebbles with seven or with eight?)
If there is no «أم», it is not permissible except according to al-Akhfash, and what is in that has preceded. It may be that he made it a pure statement, its meaning being: "why were its verses not set out in detail, so that part of them were non-Arabic, understood by non-Arabs, and part Arabic, understood by Arabs?"
Al-aʿjamī is one who does not speak clearly, even if he is of the Arabs; it is related to its quality, like «أحمرِيّ» and «دَوَّاريّ», so the yāʾ in it is for intensifying the description, and the relation in it is not real. Al-Rāzī said in his Lawāmiḥ: "It is like the yāʾ of «كُرْسِيّ» and «بُخْتِيّ»." The Shaykh distinguished between them, saying: "It is not like the yāʾ of «كُرْسِيّ», for in «كرسيّ» and «بُخْتيّ» the word is built upon it, unlike the yāʾ of «أعجميّ», for they say «رجل أَعْجم» and «أعْجميّ»."
ʿAmr ibn Maymūn read «أَعَجَمِيٌّ» with fatḥa on the ʿayn; it is related to al-ʿajam (non-Arabs), and the yāʾ in it is truly for relation; one says «رجل أعجميٌّ» (a man of non-Arab stock) even if he is eloquent. The discussion of the difference between them has preceded in Sūrat al-Shuʿarāʾ.
There are three aspects for the nominative of «أَعْجميّ». First: it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being: "are a non-Arabic and an Arabic equal?" Second: it is the predicate of an omitted subject, i.e. "it," meaning the Qurʾān, is non-Arabic while the one sent with it is Arab. Third: it is the fāʿil (agent) of an implied verb, i.e. "are a non-Arabic and an Arabic equal?" This is weak, since the verb is omitted only in places I have explained more than once.
His saying: {والذين لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ}: There are three aspects in it. First: it is a mubtadaʾ, with «في آذانِهم» its khabar and «وَقْرٌ» a fāʿil; or «في آذانهم» is a fronted predicate and «وقرٌ» a postponed subject, the clause being the predicate of the first. Second: «وَقْرٌ» is the predicate of an implied subject, and the clause is the predicate of the first, the implied form being: "and those who do not believe — it is deafness in their ears"; having reported of it that it is guidance for those, He reported of it that it is deafness in the ears of these and blindness upon them. Al-Zamakhsharī stated its meaning. There is no need for the implication when the speech is complete without it. Third: {الذين لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ} is conjoined to «الذين آمنوا», and «وَقْرٌ» is conjoined to «هدىً»; this is of the category of conjunction to the governed words of two governors, and there are doctrines about it whose analysis has preceded.
His saying: «عَمَىً»: The majority read it with fatḥa on the mīm, with tanwīn; it is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of «عَمِي يَعْمَى», like «صَدِي يَصْدَى صَدَىً» and «هَوِي يَهْوَى هَوَىً».
Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn ʿUmar, Ibn al-Zubayr and a group read «عَمٍ» with kasra and tanwīn, as a defective noun (ism manqūṣ), [the Qurʾān] being described with it figuratively. ʿAmr ibn Dīnār read — and it was transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās — «عَمِيَ» with kasra on the mīm and fatḥa on the yāʾ, as a past verb. There are two aspects regarding the pronoun, the more apparent being that it refers to the Qurʾān; the second, that it refers to the deafness, but the meaning rejects it. «في آذانهم» — if you do not make it the predicate — is attached to an omitted [word] as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from it [«وقر»], because it was originally an adjective; it is not attached to it, because it is a maṣdar, so what it governs does not precede it. His saying {وَهُوَ عَلَيْهِمْ عَمًى} is likewise in the reading of the majority; as for the two preceding readings, «على» is attached to what follows it, since it is not a maṣdar.

semin-durr:46-46.t: His saying: {فَلِنَفْسِهِ}: It may be attached to an implied verb, i.e. "for himself is his work"; and it may be the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "then the righteous deed is for himself." His saying «فعليها» is like it.

semin-durr:47-47.t:
His saying: {وَمَا تَخْرُجُ مِن ثَمَرَاتٍ}: This «ما» may be negating, which is the apparent sense, and it may be a relative; Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed that without explaining its basis. Its explanation is that it would be in the position of the genitive by conjunction to «الساعة», i.e. "knowledge of the Hour and knowledge of that which comes out," and «مِنْ ثمرات» on this would be a ḥāl (circumstantial), or «مِنْ» would be for clarification. The second «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the extent. As for the second «ما», it is negating only. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "because «ولا تَضَعُ» is conjoined to it, then the negation is broken by «إلاَّ»; had it been in the sense of «الذي», conjoined to «الساعة», that would not be permissible."
Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read «ثمرات», and what strengthens it is that it is written with the extended tāʾ.
The rest [read] «ثمرة» in the singular, meaning the genus. If «ما» is negating, «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida) in the agent; if it is a relative, it is for clarification, as has preceded.
«الأَكْمام» is the plural of «كِمّ» with kasra on the kāf — so al-Zamakhsharī vocalised it — which is what covers the fruit, like the sheath of the palm spathe. Al-Rāghib said: "Al-kumm is what covers the hand of the shirt, and what covers the fruit, and its plural is «أكْمام»." This indicates that it has ḍamma on the kāf, since he made it shared between the sleeve of the shirt and the covering of the fruit, and there is no disagreement that the sleeve of the shirt is with ḍamma. So it may be that the container of the fruit has two dialectal forms, unlike the sleeve of the shirt, reconciling their two statements. As for «أَكِمَّة», its singular is «كِمام», like «أَزِمَّة» and «زِمام». Ibn Kathīr gave fatḥa to the yāʾ of «شُركائيَ».
His saying: {مَا مِنَّا مِن شَهِيدٍ}: This negative clause suspends (taʿlīq) «آذنَّاك», because it is in the sense of «أَعْلَمْناك» (We informed you). [The poet] said:
3961 - آذَنَتْنا ببَيْنِها أسماءُ ... رُبَّ ثاوٍ يَمَلُّ منه الثَّواءُ
(Asmāʾ informed us of her parting; many a one who stays is one whose staying is wearisome.)
A disagreement has preceded for us about suspending «أعلم» ...; the correct view is that it occurs, as heard from the Arabs. Abū Ḥātim allowed a pause on «آذنَّاك» and on «ظنُّوا», beginning with the negation after them by way of resumption. «مِنَّا» is a fronted khabar (predicate) and «مِنْ شهيد» is a mubtadaʾ (subject). It is also possible that «مِنْ شهيد» is a fāʿil (agent) of the prepositional phrase before it, because it is supported by the negation.

semin-durr:48-48.t: His saying: {مَا لَهُمْ مِّن مَّحِيصٍ}: like His saying {مَا مِنَّا مِن شَهِيدٍ}, without difference.

semin-durr:49-49.t: His saying: {مِن دُعَآءِ الخير}: a maṣdar (verbal noun) annexed to its object, its agent being omitted, i.e. "he." ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] read «مِن دُعَآءِ بالخير».

semin-durr:50-50.t:
His saying: {لَيَقُولَنَّ هذا لِي}: the answer to the oath, because it precedes the condition, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, as its establishment is known. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "«ليقولَنَّ» is the apodosis, and the fāʾ is omitted." I say: this is not permissible except in poetry, as in the saying:
3962 - مَنْ يَفْعلِ الحسناتِ اللَّهُ يَشْكُرُها ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Whoever does good deeds, Allah will appreciate them …)
so much so that al-Mubarrad forbids it even in poetry, and he transmits the verse as: «فالرحمن يشكرُه».

semin-durr:52-52.t:
His saying: {قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ}: The discussion of it has preceded several times. Its first object here is omitted, its implied form being "have you considered yourselves," and the second is the interrogative clause.
«الآفاق» is the plural of «أُفُق», which is the region. The poet said:
3963 - لو نالَ حيٌّ مِن الدنيا بمنزلةٍ ... أفْقَ السماءِ لنالَتْ كفُّه الأُفُقا
(If any living being could reach, by rank in this world, the horizon of heaven, his hand would have reached the horizon.)
It is like «أَعْناق» from «عُنُق», its hamza changed into alif. Al-Rāghib transmitted that «أَفَق» is said with fatḥa on the hamza and the fāʾ, so it would be like «جَبَل» and «أَجْبال». «آفَقَ فلانٌ» means he went off into the horizons. «الآفِقُ» is one who has reached the limit of generosity, likening him in that to one who goes into the horizons. The relative adjective of «الأُفُق» is «أَفَقيٌّ» with fatḥa on both. I say: it is possible that it was related to the form with fatḥa, and they dispensed with that from relating to the form with ḍamma; and it has parallels.

semin-durr:53-53.t: His saying: {أَوَلَمْ يَكْفِ بِرَبِّكَ}: There are two aspects in it. First: the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) in the fāʿil (agent), and this is the preponderant view; the object is omitted, i.e. "does your Lord not suffice you?" In His saying {أَنَّهُ على كُلِّ شَيْءٍ شَهِيدٌ} there are two aspects. One: it is a badal (substitute) for «بربك», so it is nominative in position and genitive in form, like what it follows. The other: the origin is «بأنَّه», then the preposition was omitted, so the [known] disagreement applies. The second of the two original aspects: «بربك» is the object, and «أنه» with what follows is the agent, i.e. "does His testimony not suffice your Lord?" It has been read {إِنَّهُ على كُلِّ} with kasra, by implying [a verb of] saying, or by way of resumption.

semin-durr:54-54.t: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and al-Ḥasan read «في مُرْيَة» with ḍamma on the mīm, and it has preceded that it is a dialectal variant of the form with kasra on the mīm. And Allah knows best.
